2.title: Skip DLC Intro Popups
2.mouse: The DLCs' and Courier's Stash packs' boxes when you leave Doc Mitchell's house aren't shown (you still get everything)

4.title: Synced Radio
4.mouse: Your radios and Pip-Boy play the host's stations, in step with the host

5.title: Synced Weather
5.mouse: Outdoors with the host, friends see the host's weather. Off for a friend: that friend keeps their own. Off for the host: everyone does

6.title: Desync Notices
6.mouse: A corner message when your game and another player's disagree for a while

8.title: Friend Markers
8.mouse: A chevron and the name over each friend, so you can find them

9.title: Field of View
9.mouse: How wide you see the world (0: the game's own, 75). Your hands and weapon stay as they are

10.title: Friends' Pip-Boy Lights
10.mouse: Show the light of a friend's Pip-Boy on them when they turn it on

12.title: Show My Address
12.mouse: Switch on to see this PC's addresses for friends joining by IP (only you see them; off and on again to see them again)

13.title: Co-op Settings (the host's count for everyone)

14.title: Co-op Balanced
14.mouse: Harder and made for a group: smarter enemies, scarcer supplies, slower leveling. Leave it off if you use mods that change the game's balance

15.title: Friendly Fire
15.mouse: Players' shots and explosions can hurt each other

16.title: Areas Around Far Friends
16.mouse: When you host, the area around a friend far from you runs in your game too, so its creatures are the same for both of you. About 10 MB of memory a cell; off: they wait, held still, until you come near

17.title: Visitors' Companions
17.mouse: Friends' companions from their own saves show in the host's game and fight beside you, their hits and hurts kept in step. Off: they stay in their owners' games only, where they still follow and fight as normal

18.title: Same Companion, One Each
18.mouse: If you host and a visitor's save has the same companion as yours, you each keep your own. Off: only one shows (yours), so there are no duplicates

20.title: Send And Receive Gifts
20.mouse: Lets you send caps through the Co-op Teleporter and receive them from friends. Off: no Send caps button, and anything sent to you goes back to the sender

21.title: Save After A Gift
21.mouse: Saves everyone's game a few seconds after you receive a gift, so it can't be lost. Causes a short hitch. If you turn it off, loading an older save could lose a gift

23.title: Your Shots Fly the Same Path for Friends
23.mouse: Friends' copies of your shots follow your real shots. Off: they fly from your character's aim, as they used to

2.title: Text Chat
2.mouse: Chat lines float above the player who said them

3.title: Chat Key
3.mouse: The key that opens the chat line and history (Enter sends, Esc cancels, Page Up and Down read back)

5.title: Read Chat Out Loud
5.mouse: Chat lines are spoken from where the player is: louder near, to the side they're on

6.title: Speech Volume
6.mouse: How loud chat lines are read out

7.title: Your Voice
7.mouse: The voice everyone hears your chat lines in

8.title: Which Voice
8.mouse: If a PC has more than one voice of that kind, which one (Windows usually has one of each)

9.title: Your Voice's Pitch
9.mouse: Lower or higher than the voice's own

10.title: Your Voice's Speed
10.mouse: Slower or faster than the voice's own

11.title: Voice Effect
11.mouse: Radio: a crackly walkie-talkie. Robot: metallic. Echo. Megaphone: loud and harsh

13.title: Voice Chat
13.mouse: Talk to the others with your microphone (through Steam's voice), heard from where you are

14.title: Talk Mode
14.mouse: Push to talk: hold the key to talk. Open mic: always on (Steam leaves out the silence)

16.title: Voice Volume
16.mouse: How loud the others' voices are

17.title: Mouths Move When Talking
17.mouse: A player's character opens and shuts its mouth while they talk or their chat line is read out

2.title: Pings
2.mouse: Mark the spot you're aiming at for players near you

3.title: Ping Key
3.mouse: The key that marks the spot you're aiming at

4.title: Ping Sound
4.mouse: The sound you hear when a ping appears

5.title: Ping Range
5.mouse: How near a player must be for you to see their ping. 0 means no limit. Only changes what you see

6.title: Ping Icons
6.mouse: The icon on each ping: off, in your HUD's colour, or each kind in its own colour

7.title: Recognise Objects
7.mouse: Your pings name what you aim at and use its icon, such as loot or a workbench. Off: every ping you send is a plain marked spot

8.title: Ping Characters
8.mouse: Pinging someone puts an icon over their head that follows them: a skull for enemies, a person for anyone else. Off: it's a plain marked spot

9.title: Ping Follows Items
9.mouse: A ping on loot, such as a weapon or a Stimpak, stays on it if it's knocked, thrown or carried away. Off: it stays where the item was

2.title: Show Emotes and Songs
2.mouse: Friends see your Too Many Emotes dances and hear their songs from your character, and you see and hear theirs. Your own Too Many Emotes music switch still decides whether you hear songs. Does nothing without Too Many Emotes

3.title: Friends Dance Along With You
3.mouse: Too Many Emotes makes everyone near you dance along. On: friends' characters join in, but only on your screen (they aren't dancing in their own game). Off: only other people dance along

4.title: Join Friends' Emotes
4.mouse: Look at a friend who's emoting and press E to dance the same emote with them, in step, at any point of it. Their song keeps playing from them. You don't need to own it in The Disco Shop. Move, press E on them again, or pick an emote of your own to stop

2.title: Show Nearby Conversations
2.mouse: When a friend near you talks to someone, what they both say is listed on your screen

3.title: Preview
3.mouse: Fills the log with sample lines so you can try its position and look. Close the menu to see it. It turns itself off when a game loads

4.title: Distance
4.mouse: How close you need to be to the one talking (1500: as far as you hear them)

5.title: Lines
5.mouse: How many lines show at once

6.title: Seconds
6.mouse: How long each line stays before it fades out

8.title: Place
8.mouse: Above HP Bar: the log sits just above your HP bar and grows upward. Custom: it goes where the two sliders below say

9.title: Horizontal Position
9.mouse: With Place set to Custom: how far across the screen the log starts, in percent. It stays on screen

10.title: Vertical Position
10.mouse: With Place set to Custom: how far down the screen the log starts, in percent. It stays on screen

11.title: Width
11.mouse: How wide the log gets before a line moves down to the next one. Lower it to keep clear of other parts of the HUD

12.title: Alignment
12.mouse: Which side of the log the lines sit against. Right suits a log on the right of the screen

14.title: Text Size
14.mouse: How big the lines are, in percent

16.title: Readability
16.mouse: What helps the text read over bright places: a thin dark outline, a drop shadow or a dark bar behind it

17.title: Dividers
17.mouse: A thin line under each line

19.title: Use HUD Colour
19.mouse: Show the lines in your HUD's colour instead of the colour below

20.title: Red
20.mouse: The red in the lines' colour

21.title: Green
21.mouse: The green in the lines' colour

22.title: Blue
22.mouse: The blue in the lines' colour

2.title: Show Chat History
2.mouse: Opening chat shows recent chat and party events (Page Up and Down read further back)

3.title: Show Party Events
3.mouse: Short lines such as a friend going down, joining or leaving appear for a few seconds

4.title: Show New Messages
4.mouse: A friend's chat message shows in the panel for a few seconds without you opening chat

5.title: Preview
5.mouse: Fills the panel with sample lines, as many as it can show, so you can try its position and look. Close the menu to see it, and turn this off when you're done

6.title: Seconds
6.mouse: How long party event and new message lines stay on screen. Long messages stay a little longer

8.title: Horizontal Position
8.mouse: How far across the screen the panel's aligned side goes, in percent. It stays on screen

9.title: Vertical Position
9.mouse: How far down the screen the panel starts, in percent. It stays on screen

10.title: Width
10.mouse: How wide the panel gets before a line moves down to the next one. Lower it to keep clear of other parts of the HUD

11.title: Alignment
11.mouse: Which side of the panel the lines sit against. The horizontal position is where that side goes

13.title: Text Size
13.mouse: How big the lines are, in percent

15.title: Readability
15.mouse: What helps the text read over bright places: a thin dark outline, a drop shadow or a dark bar behind it

16.title: Dividers
16.mouse: A thin line under each line
